To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the DLP in algebraic tori of small order over finite fields can be solved by an algorithm that runs in time polynomial in the size of the input, but that this is not yet enough to threaten the security of any of the known cryptosystems based on tori.
the discrete logarithm in the groups T2(p^m) and T6(p^m) is as hard as in the multiplicative group of the field p^m for all p and m of cryptographic interest.
the discrete logarithm in the algebraic tori $T_n(\mathbb{Q}_p)$ and $T_n(\F_{q^2})$ is hard, but not as hard as previously believed.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the discrete logarithm (DL) problem on algebraic tori.
the following question: how difficult is the discrete logarithm in algebraic tori?
the discrete logarithm (DLP) problem over finite fields.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we do not know the precise security of the discrete log problem over the algebraic tori $T_k(\mathbb{Q})$ and $ T_k(\mathbb F_{p^m})$.
the security of the above mentioned cryptosystems in the tori $\mathbb{G}_2$ and $\mathbb{F}_6$ remains unproven.
we do not have a good understanding of how hard it is to solve the discrete logarithm in the groups $T_2$ and $T_{6}$, and we need further investigation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
our algorithm does not provide a practical alternative to the Pollard rho method for solving the DLP over finite fields.
the DLP in $T_2$ and $T_{6}$ over prime fields is as hard as the DLP over elliptic curves, and that the DLP over prime finite fields is harder than that over prime fields.
the security of the DLP in algebraic tori is still not well-understood.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, for certain groups, it may be more efficient to work directly in the group, as opposed to using a subgroup of the same order, and then lift to the original group.
the DLP in algebraic tori may be easier to solve than previously expected.

, for the first time, we have an algorithm for the DLP that works in the tori that is more efficient than the best known methods for the DLP over the multiplicative group of the finite field $\mathbb{F}_p$.
